materials.label: Late-Uruk accounting media at Chogha Mish
materials.what_audience_follows: Two coexisting clay accounting devices—an envelope that contains tokens and a sealed numerical tablet—show information moving from enclosed/countable objects toward marks carried on a clay surface without proving a one-line token-to-writing genealogy.
sequence: A clay envelope contains accounting tokens while sealing controls or authenticates the container.
A separate sealed numerical tablet fragment carries five numeral signs directly on a clay surface.
Both belong to the Late Uruk administrative ecology, so the audience can follow a change in where numerical information is carried while keeping multiple antecedent practices in view.

locators: Visible Language, object descriptions Catalog No. 31, p. 65: ChM III-937a, sealed numerical tablet fragment with five numeral signs
Visible Language, object description Catalog No. 32, pp. 65–66: broken clay envelope with tokens inside

limitations: The objects are from Chogha Mish in Iran, not an excavated sequence at Uruk.
Coexistence and functional similarity do not establish that one object directly evolved into the other.
Use this material to show an ecology of accounting media, not a universal token → tablet ladder.
